lines.en: : Do you have anything to do with it? Because it seems to me like you keep selecting other heroines instead.
: Who knew the woes of the childhood friend route applied to real life as well?
: You’re starting to sound like a certain Irish girl I know and I can’t say I’m a fan of it.
: Just remember that if you do continue rejecting my advances, there is an entire Facebook group of people willing to sleep with me. And most of them would probably pay.
: You get the first-love discount. That’s a once in a lifetime promotion, you know.
: Oh, I know. And I’ll be sure to capitalize on it once everything surrounding our relationship stops being so damn depressing.
: Ugh. I really am going to make it to thirty after all.
Another bout of a certain brand of silence, one that I am beginning to recognize like the back of my hand, carries across the outstretched horizon before planting itself firmly in my lap.
It curls up into a ball of intangible warmth and fills me with a dreadful nostalgia that I attempt to wish away by focusing on the head resting upon my shoulder.
I wonder if this warmth has invaded her as well — and if the thoughts inside her head at this very moment add up to more than just “I’m happy here.”
Are you?
Happiness is tricky — confusing. And people like me who have grown so disenchanted by the pursuit of it approach the word with extreme caution so as to not think we’re happy when we’re not.
So many good things have happened to me lately.
And if that is any indication of what is yet to come, I’d be a fool to not admit I’m terrified as there must always be a balance.
What goes up must always come down —but that comes with a caveat.
There are things you’ll see and experience in life that will push you further down into the bottomless pit of existence than you’d ever fall on your own.
And while there may be people who notice you screaming and begging for help — who take it upon themselves to lend you a hand and attempt to pull you up, no one will ever pull you out.
In the end, you either drag them down with you or let go and hope they never meet the same fate.
It will always be easier to fall than it will be to climb.
And when you’ve fallen as deep as I have, the last thing you possess is the willpower to fight back against fate.
So you fall...and fall...and fall forever-
: I love you so much.
And pray that the slowly vanishing light at the top of the well never fully disappears.
: I...love you too, Niki.
: Thanks for trying to pull me out of my bottomless pit.
: It’s that or I jump in there with you. Better to suffer together than to suffer alone, right?
: You don’t deserve to suffer.
: Neither do you.
: I do, though. I’m probably not the same person I was when I was with you. A lot has happened since then and I’ve done...a lot of horrible things.
: You can always change.
: See, that’s the thing...I don’t want to. And I have no idea what type of person I’d be if I did.
: I’ve become the worst parts of myself...I’ve accepted them. And getting rid of those traits would be more like me turning into a new person than turning over a new leaf.
: Then, I hope that bottomless pit of yours is wide enough for two.
: Niki-
: No matter what you’ve done or what you’ll do, I’ll be right there with you.
: You chose a really stubborn person to spend so much time with way back when. This is the result of that.
: You’re too weak to function on your own. Plus, it’s not like I have to agree with all of those “horrible things” you do, right?
: You need someone to call you out on your shit — and who better than the girl who’s dealt with more of it than anyone?
: You’re not like this because you’re a bad person, you’re like this because you never learned how to be a good one.
: It’s not your fault.
: That...doesn’t make it okay.
: Never said it did...just that I’ll always be your home when you have nowhere else to go.
: I wish I remembered more of our past together.
: I don’t understand why I ever would have left you behind.
: You left me behind because you’re a selfish asshole who's never been able to grasp the fact that there are other people out there struggling as well.
: But you’re back now. And that’s what matters most.
: We’ll return your memories one way or another- even if I have to force them in myself.
: Yeah? And how would you do that?
: You don’t have any other plans for the rest of the day, do you?
: I don’t.
: Then...let's go for a walk-

One's grand flights, one's Sunday baths,
One's tootings at the weddings of the soul
Occur as they occur. So bluish clouds
Occurred above the empty house and the leaves
Of the rhododendrons rattled their gold,
As if someone lived there. Such floods of white
Came bursting from the clouds. So the wind
Threw its contorted strength around the sky.
[[BREAK]
Could you have said the bluejay suddenly
Would swoop to earth? It is a wheel, the rays
Around the sun. The wheel survives the myths.
The fire eye in the clouds survives the gods.
To think of a dove with an eye of grenadine
And pines that are cornets, so it occurs,
And a little island full of geese and stars:
It may be the ignorant man, alone,
Has any chance to mate his life with life
That is the sensual, pearly spouse, the life
That is fluent in even the wintriest bronze.
There is a disconnect between that which is real and that which is not — but that disconnection is not one to be perceived by man.
It is visible to only those with the eyes of God and those who, in the moments of utmost unholiness, spill liquid sacrament from their pores and tongue.
There is a trip to be traveled through unmapped parts of the world.
You will see things that happened and didn’t.
You will feel things you will never feel again.
AND YOU WILL SAVOR THE SPLENDOR IN EVERY SECOND
A walk upon glass through a forest untouched brings us several steps closer to a dance with our mirrored selves.
As my eyes connect with a conveyor belt of shadows and familiar unfamiliar faces, it is my legs that wind up moving while the world around me does not.
If I could break myself in two and reform with wings I would — but as I’ve never learned to fly, I must grapple with an unbearable truth and squeeze the life from out its body.
This is then and this is now.
I remember how to make my heart move.
: Do you remember where we are?
: Would it help if I gave you a hint?
: I can’t really put my finger on it, but...
: I know I’ve been here before.
: We built a secret base here out of stuff we picked from trash cans.
: We filled it with snacks from my pantry and pretended we were an underground crime-fighting organization.
: Any time we heard a noise, we’d hide behind trees and wait for some evildoer to move through the woods, but no one ever came.
: It was a huge waste of time looking back on things if you don’t count all of the comics we read here as “being productive” but holy shit were we always so excited to come.
: Things stopped being as exciting once Noriko found out about it and we began spending less and less time here as the days went by.
: As you can see, there’s nothing left now...but this place was once really important to us.
: Ring any bells?
: Then...
: How about this-
: We spent a lot of time in the woods when we were younger...but I never really realized it until I stopped going outside.
: This was another spot we loved. Not far from here, there was a hidden path that led to a circle of abandoned gassho houses we’d sneak into to make out.
: It feels like just yesterday we were carving our names on that tree.
: Sucks I wound up coming back to scribble yours out after you left me all alone.
: Do you have your keys on you? Maybe we could make a new carving?
: You’re still interested in things like that?
: Oh, come on. Don’t tell me you’re so dead inside that you’re against a little vandalism now?
My feet are cut deeper as the forest pulls us closer to its core.
And while images of the past break their legs trying to run through the four corners of my mind, I see nothing but an endless blur and feel nothing but the blood soaking into my socks.
The one sense that does not deceive me is my hearing as I can faintly make out the sound of a pocket knife being plunged into the flesh of an ancient tree.
We’d peel away its skin and replace it with a dream — false hopes in the form of a relationship that would one day perish only to be resurrected by sheer coincidence years later.
The rest begins to flow back in.
How small her hands were back then.
The way her glasses would fog up when it got too hot.
Her long, pink hair that would stick to my clothing and get me into trouble with-
No.
Stop remembering.
: [[REDACTED]?
: Hmm...how come we never carved our names into a tree? That would have been cute.
: Hellooooo? Anybody home? You can’t just pretend you don’t see me. I know you do.
: Hey, what’s going on? Are you remembering something?
: Hah...obstinate as ever, I see. And Niki, wow! She’s so pretty now! I can’t help but feel a little jealous.
: Are you two together again?
: Does she fuck you like I did?
: Who’s better, me or her?
: Be honest. I won’t get mad.
: Hey. Talk to me. What’s-
: I remember this place.
: What? You do?
: Yeah. We would come here...and there was a...circle of houses and...we would make out...
: Yeah, but...you’re kind of just repeating what I said a couple minutes ago. Are you really sure you remember?
: Be honest. I won’t get mad.
: More...
: I need to see more...
: Take me somewhere else...
: Okay...
: We’ll go on an all-inclusive tour down memory lane...
: From where it all began...
: To where it all ended.
: Where...
: Where are we?...
: I think it’s better if you remember this one without any help.
: This place had a much more profound impact on you than it did on me, after all.
Before this, there were other places.
A convenience store where we’d stop on the way to school.
An old bus stop where we’d wait for over an hour sometimes for a ride into the urban district.
An Italian restaurant we never went inside, but always talked about how it would be nice to be able to eat there one day.
A softball field.
A community pool.
The yard of an old house where a dog used to live.
It’s gone now and a new one has taken its place.
Each of these locations spurred something inside of me to begin moving again. And slowly but surely, the faded traces of what should be mine have opened up to the idea of coming home.
So why has that all come screeching to a halt at the end of the tour?
Why am I numb again now?
Was I just caught up in the moment earlier?...Piggybacking off of Niki’s nostalgia because I’m so desperate for my own?
Or am I just suppressing something?
: You jumped.
: Do you remember?
: I don’t know...
: Take as much time as you need.
: This is the hardest part of the trip after all. And I’ve already told you-
: I’ll return your memories even if I have to force them back in myself.
: This...
: This is where it happened...
: That’s right.
: This is where your world was ripped away from you.
: You can’t only open yourself up to the good memories, you have to let the bad ones in too.

: You’ll never move on if you just keep ignoring the things that make you hurt. You have to work if you ever want to get better. Only then will you be able to look back on the past without breaking into a million pieces.
: But I promise you, and I mean this with all of my heart, I will be there every...single...step of the way.
: You’re not alone...
: Look at me.
: You’re not alone.
: Okay?
: No matter how horrible you become...or how much work it takes to get you through a single day without feeling sorry for yourself...
: I will be here. I’ve always been here.
: You’re my best friend in the whole entire world...and I am so...so sorry you had to go through what you did...
: But...
: I don’t want to watch you suffer anymore...
: I want my friend back...
: Will you please stop running? Both literally and figuratively?
: Please?...
: You really won’t leave?
: Of course not. Never.
: No matter what I become?
: No matter what you become.
: Because I’m a fucking idiot.
: But I’m your fucking idiot. And you’re my big, melancholic doofus.
: So let’s go be stupid together...far away from the places that make us hurt.
: Let’s go somewhere quiet...and comfortable...
: Let’s go home, Akira...
Akira...
That’s...my name.
My name is Akira.
I’m a good boy.
